findings.reason: Verified in the migration: line 11 indexes `[0]['id']` on the embed_category join with no row check, and since the removed default means no site_settings row exists on most installs, pg's `[0]` raises IndexError, aborting the migration before the fallback on line 15 runs.

Verified that line 25 inserts the raw setting line without stripping scheme or path, while record_for_host compares against the bare `uri.host`, so migrated values like `http://eviltrout.com` can never match; the SQL interpolation also breaks on quotes.

Confirmed the regex permits `:port` and before_validation keeps it, while record_for_host compares against `uri.host` without port, so such a host saves but never matches; the TLD `{2,5}` limit is a real but narrower restriction.
Server maps a null category to uncategorized and the client sets category from the locally chosen null via findById, so the badge is empty until reload; a real but cosmetic UI glitch.
The delete chain has no catch, so a failed request leaves the row silently; correct but a minor UX gap on an admin-only action.
`where(id:).first` returning nil does lead to NoMethodError (500) and a missing host param raises on nil, but these are admin-only inputs with minor impact, so it is input-validation hardening.
No uniqueness constraint exists on host and record_for_host uses an unordered `.first`, so duplicates produce arbitrary category assignment; plausible but requires admin-created duplicates.
The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' example no longer exercises host logic, and the nested-describe Fabricate sits outside that example, so the test name is misleading; a test-quality nit.
The diff confirms category_fabricator.rb holds the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators, a naming mismatch with no functional effect.
Verified the pretender ignores the id and always returns fruits[0], so `find('fruit', 2)` actually tests apple; the test is misleading but still exercises hydration of embedded ids.

The map on a null `*_ids` value would throw and unresolved ids would produce undefined entries, and `hydrated || []` is indeed dead code, but whether the API sends null or unresolved ids is unverified.
String.replace with a string pattern does replace only the first underscore, but no current ADMIN_MODELS entry has two underscores, so this is a hypothetical future concern.
Verified the PUT route and controller `update` only re-render state, and saveChanges is not referenced by any template, so these are dead, misleading no-op paths.
